title: Sell Mineral Rights in Burgettstown, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Burgettstown, PA | Offer Today
metaDescription: Burgettstown mineral owners: understand your royalty statement and get a straightforward cash offer for your Marcellus interest.
heroLead: Burgettstown is one of the bigger names on this corner of the map, home to the amphitheater most Pittsburghers know as Star Lake, and to a fair amount of leased Marcellus acreage besides.
intro: Burgettstown is a real town, not only a crossroads, and it sits in a part of Washington County that's had steady oil and gas leasing activity going back to the early Marcellus years. If you own minerals here, chances are your family land was leased sometime in the mid-2000s to early 2010s when landmen were working the Cross Creek corridor hard, and you've been receiving a royalty tied to that original lease ever since.
We know what it's like to hold minerals passed down through a family and never get a straight explanation of what they're actually worth. That's the entire reason this business exists.

sections.heading: What's under Burgettstown-area land
paragraphs: This stretch of Washington County sits in the wet-gas Marcellus window, with operators including Range Resources and CNX Resources holding substantial leasehold in the surrounding townships. Wells here typically produce a mix of natural gas and natural gas liquids, and that liquids content is part of why post-production deductions on local royalty statements can run higher than what an owner in a purely dry-gas county would see.
Deeper Utica and Point Pleasant potential also exists under much of this ground, though most current production comes from the Marcellus interval.

sections.heading: The Act 13 impact fee and what it actually pays for
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Act 13 impact fee is collected on unconventional wells and distributed to counties and municipalities, including ones like Burgettstown, to help offset the local costs of drilling activity: road wear, emergency services, environmental programs. It's separate from your royalty and doesn't reduce what you're owed, but it's part of the same larger picture of how this state, unlike most other gas-producing states, chose a flat per-well fee instead of a production severance tax. Owners often ask about it when they're trying to understand why Pennsylvania's system feels different from what they hear about in Texas or Oklahoma.

sections.heading: What we check before you decide anything
paragraphs: We trace title through the Washington County Recorder of Deeds, confirm your net mineral acreage and decimal interest against the relevant unit, and review your recent royalty statements before putting together an offer. You'll see exactly how we got to the number.

faqs.question: Does the Act 13 impact fee come out of my royalty?
faqs.answer: No. The impact fee is paid by the operator directly to the state and distributed to counties and municipalities. It's separate from, and doesn't reduce, your royalty payment.

faqs.question: Why is my deduction line bigger than I expected?
faqs.answer: Wet-gas areas like Burgettstown route production through liquids processing before your royalty is calculated, and that processing cost is typically netted against your check under current Pennsylvania case law.

faqs.question: How long does an offer stay valid?
faqs.answer: We'll tell you upfront when we send a number, but you're never pressured to decide on the spot.
